title: Facet joint forces
summary: Apply each pure moment, compression or combined load and report the facet contact force, or the share of axial load carried by the facets.
simulate: Build the specimen named in the task (FSU or multi-level lumbar spine); keep facet capsules unless stated.
Fix the caudal end; apply the pure moment (swept over the listed moments), axial load or imposed rotation of the simulation.
Facet force = compressive contact force (N, positive) on the facet named in the task: right, loaded or mean of both.
Loaded facet: the compressed one (ipsilateral in lateral bending, contralateral in axial rotation, both in extension).
Report every output as one curve over the sweep, or one number where there is no sweep. Facet share = total facet force normal to the disc plane / axial force x 100.

All values come from the primary papers; the Ghezelbash 2020 review compilation was checked against them and its errors corrected (see each test's check_notes).
Schendel peaks are the largest single values printed, not means. Excluded: sensor-calibration and capsule-strain studies.
agent_prompt: Use your finite element lumbar spine model. Run the 35 simulations in `simulations`. Fix the caudal end and apply the load of each simulation: pure moment (swept where a sweep is given), axial or follower compression, eccentric compression, or an imposed rotation. Report facet contact force in N, compressive positive: right or mean of both facets in flexion-extension, the loaded facet in lateral bending (ipsilateral) and axial rotation (contralateral). facet_share = total facet (or neural-arch) force as % of the applied axial force; facet_slope = slope of right-facet force vs applied moment (N/Nm). Schendel 1993 slope simulations (L1-L2 FSU, 300 N creep preload): flexion/extension by 75-300 N compression at 1-4 cm lever arms (up to ~12 Nm), lateral bending by 50-200 N cable loads (up to ~3 Nm), axial rotation through a 5.5 cm lever with 150 N axial load. Specimens: Jaramillo L4-S1 without facet capsules; Wiseman L2-L5 without capsules; Botolin T12-S1 with a 400 N follower load; Lorenz, Yang & King, Pollintine, Farooq and Rousseau are single FSUs ('lumbar FSU': use L4-L5). Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
